clue.text: Settee getting mucked up with choc, over time, and other food

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit over, that is all around, the word for time
mucked up means messed about, so the letters of settee and choc are jumbled together

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A sofa gets smeared with chocolate as time passes, alongside some other foodstuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mucked up' makes COTTCHEESE, and 'over' means that jumble sits around the time word. Choc is itself a food, which is why the definition reads 'other food'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cottage cheese is a soft curd dairy product, a foodstuff distinct from the chocolate already mentioned.

clue.text: Disgusting and rotten final scene?

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotten
the ending of a play or film is its final scene

explanation.surface: A critic finds the last scene of a play both repellent and badly done.
explanation.definitionFit: Something offending the senses is repellent, the sense the clue's adjective carries.

clue.text: Athenian contributing to testimonial

indicators.note: the answer contributes letters to the longer word, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A citizen of ancient Athens adds his word to a tribute.
explanation.walkthrough: TIMON of Athens is the misanthrope of Shakespeare's play, a legendary Athenian.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon was a wealthy citizen of ancient Athens, famed through Plutarch and Shakespeare for his misanthropy.

clue.text: Girl with fancy shoes for footwear

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

indicators.note: fancy here means fanciful or reworked, so the letters of shoes are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman with stylish shoes is choosing what to wear on her feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Galoshes are waterproof overshoes, a kind of footwear worn over ordinary shoes.

clue.text: Happy shout full of explosive energy

indicators.note: the word for shout is filled with the other letters, which sit inside it

parts.note: to cry is to shout out
HE stands for high explosive
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A joyful yell bursting with dynamic vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cheery is in good spirits, cheerful and glad.

clue.text: English doctor exceptionally caring and welcoming

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests something done out of the ordinary way, so the letters of caring are rearranged

explanation.surface: An English physician is praised as unusually kind and warmly receptive.
explanation.definitionFit: Embracing an idea or person means accepting it warmly, being receptive or hospitable to it.

clue.text: Woman has turned up to hug artist

indicators.note: the word has hugs the artist's letters, holding them inside
in a down entry, turned up means the letters read from bottom to top, so the whole piece is written backwards

parts.note: taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A woman arrives and embraces a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hug' gives HARAS, and 'turned up' reads it bottom to top, as fits a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah is a common female first name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Anger consumed individual outside front of zoo: "it's an unnatural environment for penguins!"

definitions.text: it's an unnatural environment for penguins!

parts.note: a temper is a fit of anger
to have consumed something is to have eaten it

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: outside here means just beyond, so the word for individual comes after the letter from zoo

explanation.surface: A zookeeper fumes that a warm enclosure is no proper home for penguins.
explanation.walkthrough: Most penguins live in cold southern waters, so the mild belt between tropics and polar regions is not their natural habitat; the definition is a playful one.
explanation.definitionFit: The temperate zone is the mild climatic belt between tropics and polar circles, warmer than the icy home of most penguins.

clue.text: A game — commercial type producing criticism

parts.note: nim is a game of taking objects from heaps
an ad is a commercial or advertisement
a version is a type or variant of something

explanation.surface: A game, an advert, a variant: a list that somehow leads to censure.
explanation.walkthrough: NIM is a mathematical game in which players take turns removing objects from heaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Animadversion is a formal word for censure or critical comment.

clue.text: With the folks in Paris, say

definitions.text: With the folks in Paris, say

parts.words: With the folks in Paris, say
parts.note: the phrase for being at home with one's relatives, as a French speaker would put it

explanation.definitionFit: The French expression means at home with the family, informally or among one's own people.

clue.text: Peer totally unproductive from what we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word for unproductive is said aloud, sounding like the answer

parts.note: barren land produces nothing at all

explanation.surface: A lord who achieves nothing at all, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a member of the peerage, the lowest rank of British nobleman.

clue.text: Metal peg attached to small tree

parts.note: a pin is a slender metal peg
on means fixed to or attached to

explanation.surface: A metal spike is fixed to a sapling.
explanation.definitionFit: The piñon is a small pine of the American south-west, grown for its edible nuts.

clue.text: Source of pleasure in fraudulent part of London

indicators.note: the treat goes inside the word for fraudulent

parts.note: sham means fake or fraudulent
a treat is something that gives delight

explanation.surface: A delight found in a crooked corner of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: STREATHAM is a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Streatham is a district in south London, so it is one area of the city.

clue.text: Animal about to get in river by edge of moor

parts.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written
the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England

indicators.note: the edge of the word here is its last letter

explanation.surface: A creature is on the point of wading into a river beside the moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: The reindeer is an Arctic deer, a large herding mammal of the far north.

clue.text: One's spotted boy standing on head (dull boy)

indicators.note: a word upside down in a down entry reads from the bottom up, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy
matt or mat means without shine, dull
Ian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad upside down on his head beside a lacklustre youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing on head' turns LAD upside down to DAL; MAT is a variant spelling of matt, lacking shine.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dalmatian is a dog breed famous for its white coat with black or liver spots.

clue.text: Something to drink? Litre's one pound

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a litre
the Roman numeral I is one
a quid is British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: A litre of something costs a single pound.
explanation.walkthrough: QUID is everyday British slang for a pound coin or note.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid is any fluid substance, and drinks are fluids.

clue.text: General slave, I run, having broken free

indicators.note: breaking free suggests the letters escape their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A captive general flees, having escaped his chains.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal means applying everywhere or to all, which is the sense of general as an adjective.

clue.text: Priest's chair — it somehow hides end of aisle

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hide the extra letter inside them
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters of chair and it are reorganised
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A clergyman's seat somehow conceals the far end of the church aisle.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieratic means relating to priests, as in the cursive script used by ancient Egyptian clergy.

clue.text: Leg got entangled in fastener

indicators.note: entangled means twisted up, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Someone's leg got caught up in a clasp.
explanation.definitionFit: A toggle is a short bar or peg passed through a loop to fasten a coat.

clue.text: Calls one journalist back from area close to fight

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: back means the word for journalist is written in the reverse direction

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter phones in from just beside a boxing bout.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringside is the area right next to a boxing ring, closest to the bout.

clue.text: Sound honest on the radio

indicators.note: speech over the airwaves is heard, not seen, so the word for honest is spoken

parts.note: straight means frank and honest

explanation.surface: A broadcaster comes across as truthful when heard on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound is a narrow channel of sea between two landmasses, which is also what a strait is.

clue.text: Prophet who cooks beef in Tibet?

parts.note: a zo is a yak-cattle hybrid of the Himalayas, so Tibetan beef
a roaster is one who cooks by roasting

explanation.surface: A Himalayan chef roasting yak meat is cast as a holy seer.
explanation.walkthrough: The ZO (also dzo or zho) is a cross between yak and domestic cattle in Tibet and nearby regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoroaster was the ancient Persian founder of Zoroastrianism, revered as a prophet.

clue.text: A person in authority upset member of a religion

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: a tsar is an autocratic ruler, or now any official given sweeping powers

explanation.surface: An official finds himself upset by a believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the whole of A plus TSAR, reading ATSAR backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rasta is a follower of Rastafarianism, a faith that originated in Jamaica.

clue.text: Revolutionary fighting force in activity aimed at downfall of a king

definitions.text: activity aimed at downfall of a king

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary force

explanation.surface: A rebel joins an armed unit in a plot to topple the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the object is checkmate, trapping the opposing king, so it is a game whose goal is his overthrow.

clue.text: Island that's cold nearly all of the month

parts.note: C stands for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: nearly all means the last letter of the month is removed

parts.note: April is the month meant here

explanation.surface: An isle that stays chilly for almost the whole of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly all of' drops the final L of APRIL, leaving APRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples, off the south-west coast of Italy.

clue.text: Type of American citizen that is wrong to head west

indicators.note: in an across entry heading west means reading right to left, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: An immigrant category in the United States considered mistaken for those going west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to head west' reverses IESIN as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Nisei are American-born children of Japanese immigrants, a category of US citizen.

clue.text: An amount collected by the waiter in connection with one part of meal

parts.note: taken as written
a tip is the gratuity a waiter collects
as to means concerning or in connection with

explanation.surface: A waiter pockets a gratuity for serving one course of a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian starter course of cold meats and vegetables, one course of a meal.

clue.text: An attractive region

parts.note: attractive in the sense of exerting a pull on iron, around a magnet, not in the sense of pretty

explanation.definitionFit: A magnetic field is the space around a magnet where its force of attraction acts.
